title: Histone H3 Methylation Dynamics During Giardia lamblia Encystation Reveal an Unexpected Association Between H3K36 me3 and Peripheral Vacuoles
content: Giardia lamblia undergoes encystation to form environmentally resistant cysts, a process involving extensive cellular remodeling and changes in gene expression. Although histone post-translational modifications contribute to chromatin regulation in eukaryotes, their dynamics and subcellular distribution during G. lamblia differentiation remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated selected histone H3 methylation marks in proliferating trophozoites and during encystation using immunofluorescence microscopy, complemented by super-resolution imaging, Western blotting, and immunogold transmission electron microscopy. Quantitative analysis revealed modification-specific changes in nuclear fluorescence intensity. H3K4 me1 and H3K4 me3 decreased significantly at 48h, whereas H3K4 me2 decreased at both 24 and 48h. H3K36 me2 remained relatively stable, while H3K36 me3 showed reduced nuclear fluorescence at both time points. In contrast, H3K9 me3 nuclear fluorescence increased significantly at 48h. In addition to these nuclear changes, both H3K4 me3 and H3K3 6me3 exhibited peripheral cytoplasmic immunoreactivity. Further investigation of H3K36 me3 using super-resolution microscopy and immunogold transmission electron microscopy supported its association with peripheral vacuoles (PVs) in encysting cells. These findings reveal distinct patterns of histone H3 methylation-associated signals during G. lamblia encystation and identify an unexpected association of H3K36 me3 with the parasite's endolysosomal system, raising new questions about the intracellular distribution and fate of modified histone-associated material.
